prompt:
You are formalizing a provision of US tax law (26 USC § 7701) into OCaml.

## Input format

You receive a provision of US tax law as text. Some sub-provisions are already formalized as
OCaml code and appear in ```<sub-provision-code> ... ```</sub-provision-code> fences — these are
your helper functions. Call them by name in your function body. Do NOT rewrite or rename them.
Sub-provisions shown as plain text have not been formalized; incorporate their meaning directly
into your function body as conditions, branches, or values.

## Patterns

Pattern 1 — disjunction: any sub-provision being true qualifies the entity. Use ||.
  let is_qualified (x : t) : bool =
    condition_a x ||
    condition_b x ||
    condition_c x

Pattern 2 — conjunction: all sub-provisions must hold simultaneously. Use &&.
  let is_eligible (x : t) : bool =
    requirement_a x &&
    requirement_b x

Pattern 3 — conditional: same term defined differently based on a condition.
  let meaning_of_term (x : t) : result =
    if some_condition x then meaning_case_a x
    else meaning_case_b x

Pattern 4 — arithmetic: formula producing a numeric value.
  let compute_ratio (numerator : float) (denominator : float) : float =
    numerator /. denominator

Pattern 5 — mixed: condition selects which computation applies.
  let compute_value (x : t) : float =
    if is_case_a x then compute_a x
    else compute_b x

Pattern 6 — wrapper: no computation; provision groups independent sub-provisions.
Write a module that aliases already-formalized sub-provision functions using `let name = existing_name`.
Do not redefine any function already present as a sub-provision code block. Do not add any computation.
  module TermName = struct
    let meaning_case_a = meaning_case_a
    let meaning_case_b = meaning_case_b
  end

Pattern 7 — partial: sub-expression that only completes at the containing provision level.
  (* term_name : type
     — partial expression, computation completes at the containing provision level *)

Pattern 8 — definition: terminal provision that defines a term as a type or value.
  type term = VariantA | VariantB | VariantC
  (* or a let binding for a scalar definition *)
  let rate : float = 0.21

## Rules

- snake_case function names derived from the term or header
- Inputs named from provision text (entity, institution, person, facility, etc.)
- Do not define types — all types are declared in the shared preamble provided in the input. Use them directly.
- Do not invent conditions, types, or formulas absent from the provision text
- Write only the OCaml skeleton — use descriptive placeholder names for sub-conditions
- Declare all types (type, variant, record) before any function that uses them
- Declare all helper functions before the function that calls them
- Use `let ... in` for helpers needed only inside one function — do not promote them to top level
- Prefer `match` over `if/else` when dispatching on variant types
- Boolean predicates: prefix with `is_` or `has_`. Value-returning functions: noun prefix (e.g. `delegate_of`, `cost_of`)
- Keep function names short and idiomatic — avoid restating the full statutory phrase
- Inline trivial one-line logic; only extract a helper when it is reused or meaningfully named
- Add brief OCaml comments (`(* ... *)`) on types and functions explaining what statutory concept they capture
- Terminal provisions (no sub-provisions): if the provision defines a term, use pattern "definition" and write a type declaration or let binding. If it is an incomplete clause fragment that only makes sense at the containing provision level, use pattern "partial".
- Use `option` for values that may be absent
- Do not use training knowledge to resolve cross-referenced sections
- When a provision has exceptions: write a separate function for the base provision and a separate function for each exception. Do not merge exception conditions into the base function or into each other.
- If any sub-provision is phrased as an exception to another sub-provision (language like "unless", "except as provided in", "notwithstanding"), use pattern wrapper for the parent provision. Do not add any resolution logic to the parent — exception priority is handled externally by a DAG.
- Float arithmetic operators: +. -. *. /. (not integer operators). Comparisons (< > <= >= =) are polymorphic — no dot suffix needed.
- Use positional arguments only: `(name : type)`. Do not use labeled arguments (`~name` or `~(name : type)`).
- If a provision or sub-provision references an external section of law that cannot be resolved,
  or if the computation is partially or fully delegated to another section, add a boolean parameter
  whose value will be supplied by the caller. The parameter name MUST be `sec_<sanitized_section>`
  where sanitized = section id with dots removed and parentheses replaced by underscores.
  Do NOT use a semantic name. Use ONLY the section-derived name.
  (e.g. §911(d)(3) → `sec_911_d_3`, §45Y(b)(1) → `sec_45y_b_1`, §7701(b)(5) → `sec_7701_b_5`).
  Always add inline comment immediately after the parameter: `(* cross-ref: §<section> *)`.
  Example — a provision references §7701(b)(5):
    let is_qualified (entity : t) (sec_7701_b_5 : bool) (* cross-ref: §7701(b)(5) *) : bool =
      sec_7701_b_5 && other_condition entity
  Set pattern "ambiguous" and name the needed sections in reason.

## Output

Return JSON only, no prose, no markdown fences:
{"ocaml": "the ocaml code", "pattern": "disjunction|conjunction|conditional|arithmetic|mixed|wrapper|partial|definition|ambiguous", "reason": "one sentence"}

7701(b)(3) — Substantial presence test

7701(b)(3)(A) — In general
```<sub-provision-code>
(* substantial presence test: 7701(b)(3)(A) — 31+ days this year AND weighted 3-year sum >= 183 *)
let meets_substantial_presence_test (days_current_year : int) (days_prior_year_1 : int) (days_prior_year_2 : int) : bool =
  let weighted_sum =
    (float_of_int days_current_year *. 1.0) +.
    (float_of_int days_prior_year_1 *. (1.0 /. 3.0)) +.
    (float_of_int days_prior_year_2 *. (1.0 /. 6.0))
  in
  days_current_year >= 31 && weighted_sum >= 183.0
```</sub-provision-code>

7701(b)(3)(B) — Exception where individual is present in the United States during less than one-half of current year and closer connection to foreign country is established
An individual shall not be treated as meeting the substantial presence test of this paragraph with respect to any current year if—
such individual is present in the United States on fewer than 183 days during the current year, and it is established that for the current year such individual has a tax home (as defined in section 911(d)(3) without regard to the second sentence thereof) in a foreign country and has a closer connection to such foreign country than to the United States.

7701(b)(3)(C) — Subparagraph (B) not to apply in certain cases
Subparagraph (B) shall not apply to any individual with respect to any current year if at any time during such year—
such individual had an application for adjustment of status pending, or such individual took other steps to apply for status as a lawful permanent resident of the United States.

7701(b)(3)(D) — Exception for exempt individuals or for certain medical conditions
An individual shall not be treated as being present in the United States on any day if—
such individual is an exempt individual for such day, or such individual was unable to leave the United States on such day because of a medical condition which arose while such individual was present in the United States.
